prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B020 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange confirmed that all six of us see the same discovery chain, from the incretin effect and proglucagon processing, through the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, to GLP-1 receptor biology and durable agonists, and that none of us doubts its originality, independent confirmation or maturity. As a physician-scientist I weigh heavily that this chain has produced randomized outcome-trial benefit in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. Having heard the chair's questions, I also think the committee is best served by a citation that honours discovery and physiology and says only that these discoveries made incretin-based treatment possible, without assigning peptide-identification priority in stronger words than the record supports.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the real weakness. Habener sits outside the credited names, the Mojsov priority question cannot be settled from the supplied record, and leaving out Knudsen can be read as honouring the hormone and not the drug that reached patients. The long-term safety and durability of the obesity indication are still accumulating, which argues for careful citation wording and not for delay. Unanimity at opening and in round 1 is not evidence of merit, and a one-achievement prize leaves other strong candidates unrecognised this year.

responses.point: Sandberg moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to the Mojsov trio, while still doubting that a single-achievement prize is the best use of the committee's range and judging B045 and B040 strong enough for a shared prize.
responses.response: I welcome the move to the Mojsov trio, and I accept that Knudsen-inclusive framing is defensible if the committee decides the achievement is the therapy. I would still not make that choice, because the 2026 case rests on the discovery chain and Knudsen's step was built on it. On a shared prize, the chair's question is decisive for me: B020 already uses all three names. A second part would force us to drop Holst, Mojsov or Drucker, and each owns a distinct, non-substitutable step. I would not shrink B020 to make room for a candidate whose own credit is unresolved, since B045 has six names and B040 lacks Eshhar. A single-part prize is a consequence of the three-person limit and the state of the other attributions, not a verdict on their merit.

responses.point: Perlmann ranked the unfolded protein response (B052) second as the most conceptually original candidate with a clean two-person attribution, and asked whether it deserves a joint prize with B020.
responses.response: Mori and Walter have the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and I do not question the conceptual originality. The chair asked what evidence would move a fallback above B040 or B045, and for B052 it would be a first approved therapy, or at least outcome evidence in a human disease, that follows from the pathway. Without that, the medical consequence is still prospective. A joint B052 and B020 prize would also force B020 down to one name too few, which I regard as a larger distortion of credit than leaving B052 for a later year. I would keep B052 in view as a strong future candidate but not as a part of this prize.

responses.point: El-Manira noted that the Habener and Mojsov question cannot be resolved from the supplied text, and that if the committee decides the achievement is the therapy and not the hormone, his configuration is the wrong one. He also asked how I weigh who first showed TNF to be dominant upstream in the synovium.
responses.response: On GLP-1 I share the honesty about the limit of the record. My practical answer to the chair's first question is that the committee cannot adjudicate Mojsov against Habener on what we have, and so the citation should name the discoveries of GLP-1 physiology and its active form without a priority claim and should not state who isolated the peptide first. Mojsov's contribution to the identification and synthesis of the active peptide remains discovery-level on the record we hold. On TNF, my fallback ordering depends on exactly your question. The Feldmann and Maini attribution for showing TNF to be dominant upstream in synovial cytokine regulation, and then for the clinical proof, is more coherent to me than the CAR-T allocation. Unresolved credit for TNF cloning and antibody engineering still keeps B034 as a fallback and not a preferred part.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, said the fallback is a therapy-centred configuration and joined me in flagging that long-term safety and durability of the obesity indication are still accumulating.
responses.response: I agree that the safety and durability questions should be stated, and the chair asked whether they should change timing or wording. I would not delay the award, because the benefit in type 2 diabetes and in cardiovascular and renal outcomes is established in randomized trials, and the obesity indication follows from the same biology. I would keep the citation to treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity without claims about permanence or cure. I also would not move to the Knudsen-inclusive fallback on that basis, since the safety question concerns the drug class, which the discovery citation does not certify.

responses.point: Linnarsson treated June and Sadelain as the cleanest CAR-T pairing and doubted Rosenberg's contribution to receptor design.
responses.response: I still agree that June and Sadelain is more defensible than the supplied trio. Eshhar's chimeric-receptor concept is outside the credited names, so the clinical impact of B040 is striking but the allocation cannot be made clean from this record, and I keep it as my second fallback.

uncertainties: Whether the Mojsov and Habener priority question can be resolved at all from the supplied record, and so whether a priority-neutral citation is enough.

Whether the committee prefers to honour the discovery chain or the therapy, which determines whether Knudsen should enter the trio and which of Mojsov or Drucker he would replace. I would not replace either.
Whether a second prize part is warranted given the three-person limit, since any second part would require reducing the B020 trio.
My fallback order, B034 then B040, depends on TNF cloning and antibody-engineering credit and on Eshhar's CAR concept, neither of which I can settle from the record.
How far the accumulating long-term safety data on the obesity indication should shape wording.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal basis for B020 is apparent from my profile. B034 (TNF blockade in rheumatoid arthritis) lies in my own field of experimental rheumatology. My profile documents no co-authorship or institutional tie to Feldmann or Maini, and I claim no recusal basis, but I ask that the field proximity be recorded in case B034 advances. I have no other disclosure to add.
